newsitem.title: USA: Shell downplays reports of $10 bln Gulf spending.
newsitem.headline: Shell downplays reports of $10 bln Gulf spending.

text.p: Shell Oil Co, the U.S. subsidiary of the Royal Dutch/Shell Group on Thursday downplayed British newspaper reports that it plans to spend $10 billion on Gulf of Mexico oilfield development in the next few years.
"The deepwater has been a very successful area for us and we anticipate a high level of expenditure to continue, however we cannot confirm the $10 billion figure," Shell Oil said in a statement.
Reports in Thursday's Financial Times and the Times of London said Shell planned to invest $10 billion in deepwater projects over the next four or so years.

A Shell official said that the actual 1997 development expenditure figure would be made public "shortly." Royal Dutch/Shell senior executives are due to make a day-long presentation to analysts on Friday, the first such meeting in three years.

On deep-water Gulf development, the Shell statement said: "We have announced 10 discoveries. We have 12 other discoveries in various stages of evaluation which we are not prepared to talk about yet with specifics," Shell said in a statement.

The 10 announced discoveries are Augur, Tahoe, Popeye, Southeast Tahoe, Cardoman, Mars, Mensa, Ram-Powell, Ursa and Troika. Those fields are estimated to have recoverable reserves of close to 1.9 billion barrels of oil equivalent, with the Mars field by far the largest.
Capital development expenditure in the Gulf deepwater projects is $2.2 billion to date, Shell said. The company began acquiring leases in the early 1980s.
